messages:
olivia: Heads-up — automated scan flagged multiple Go module issues in our prod graph: CVE-2025-3271 affecting google.golang.org/grpc and CVE-2025-4022 affecting github.com/golang-jwt/jwt. Impacted services: inference-runtime, api-gateway. Links: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-3271 , https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-4022

security-bot: [auto-alert] Dependency scanner found vulnerable modules referenced by our repos. Created SEC-1123. See attached evidence and dependency tree.

raj: Which exact versions do we have in our monorepo? I pulled a quick go.mod snapshot:```
module github.com/redwood/inference

require (
    google.golang.org/grpc v1.54.0
    github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.0.0
)
```
These look out of date.

sam: Confirmed via `go list -m all` — grpc@v1.54.0 shows up transitively via google-cloud-storage client in infra libs; jwt@v4.0.0 is direct in authz-service. net/http itself is fine, but some higher-level usages (custom transport/timeouts) may need review for regressions after bumps.

maria: Triage notes from quick read: grpc (CVE-2025-3271) is high priority — possible remote crash/RCE in header parsing under certain options. jwt CVE-2025-4022 rated medium — signature validation edgecase with older key types. Proposed plan: 1) bump grpc to v1.58.1 (contains backported patch) and run canary on staging dedicated pool; 2) bump golang-jwt to v4.2.1 and add stricter signature validation/unit tests. I'll draft PRs unless someone objects.

raj: +1 to bump. For reproducibility, prefer explicit `go get` pins in the service modules rather than `replace` unless we must. Commands I will run in the PR:```
# bump grpc
go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.58.1
# verify sums
go mod tidy && go mod verify
```
Also we should add a brief comment in the PR about why the version was chosen and link to SEC-1123.

olivia: Also note: KMS/key rotation interactions — if we rotate signing keys we may see a spike in signature validation failures. Do not rotate KMS keys until after jwt patch is deployed and we have audit hooks in place. @maria can you own the KMS + audit plan?

maria: I can take KMS. Plan: block rotation, add audit events for all token signature failures, and create an alert if failures > 0.5% over 5m after deploy. Logging format (simple):```
log.Printf("authz.signature_failure service=%s user=%s alg=%s token_kid=%s reason=%s", svc, user, alg, kid, reason)
```
I'll add that to authz-service and wire to the security-dash.

sam: Testing checklist I'll own: - unit tests for malformed tokens and old-kid handling - e2e hitting grpc endpoints with crafted headers - load-run of grpc v1.58.1 on staging to check latency/regressions. I'll also smoke test net/http client timeouts since we use custom transports.

security-bot: [ticket update] SEC-1123 created and PR placeholders linked: PR#TBD (grpc bump), PR#TBD (jwt bump).

olivia: Action items & timeline: 1) raj open grpc bump PR + request eng-runtime review and label canary/grpc-58 — run canary on staging dedicated pool. 2) sam add tests and load-run. 3) maria own KMS/audit and create alert dashboard. Deadline: EOD tomorrow for PRs opened; canary to run overnight. :alarm_clock:

raj: On it. I'll open the grpc PR in ~30m and tag @eng-runtime and @eng-security for reviews. Will include `go mod` diffs and CI signals.

maria: I'll prepare the audit schema and alert runbook. Will not rotate keys until we confirm jwt bump deployed.

sam: I'll start test work now, aim to push test branch by tomorrow afternoon. Will report latency numbers after load-run.

olivia: Thanks team. Once canary metrics are green I'll approve and we can coordinate the rollout to prod with a short maintenance window. If anything unexpected shows up, abort and revert to previous module via go.mod replace and open rollback PR.
